correctness.rationale: The full affine Gram matrix on normalized centrally symmetric volume is diag(1,Sigma), so its exact kernel is 1+x^T Sigma^-1 y. Convexity forces evaluation maxima at vertices. The cross-polytope first marginal has Beta density d(1-|t|)^(d-1)/2 and variance 2/((d+1)(d+2)); exact integration produces the stated closed norm. On the cube, independent uniform coordinates and the Irwin-Hall CDF give the displayed exact positive-part finite sum. Equality in dimensions 1 and 2 and strict gaps for 3..12 are certified by exact rational arithmetic. For all d>=13, the cross norm exceeds d/2 while the cube norm is at most sqrt(1+3d), and these bounds are strictly separated. The cross asymptotic is immediate and the cube central limit passage follows from uniform L2 boundedness. A standalone script passed 365 checks, including independent small-d quadratures. The positivity defect is (Lambda-1)/2 by kernel normalization, not a separate unproved assertion.

value.rationale: Sharp L∞ operator norms of local L2 least-squares projections quantify worst-case amplification and loss of positivity. The cube/cross-polytope polar pair is a canonical natural object, and the result determines every dimensional constant in explicit finite form, the precise equality-to-strict boundary at dimension three, and the diverging factor sqrt(pi*d/24). These results are not merely small numerical improvements or a chosen finite slice: the theorem settles the complete integer-dimension comparison and exhibits a structural difference between polar geometries even at polynomial degree one.
